q: Upgrade the control-plane node `cp1` of a kubeadm cluster from v1.36.x to v1.37.1. Workloads must be moved off the node while its kubelet is upgraded, and the node must be schedulable again afterwards.
a:
```bash
ssh cp1
sudo -i
# point apt at the v1.37 repo (one repo per minor on pkgs.k8s.io)
sed -i 's#/v1.36/#/v1.37/#' /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kubernetes.list
apt-mark unhold kubeadm && apt-get update && apt-get install -y kubeadm='1.37.1-*' && apt-mark hold kubeadm
kubeadm version
kubeadm upgrade plan
kubeadm upgrade apply v1.37.1

kubectl drain cp1 --ignore-daemonsets
apt-mark unhold kubelet kubectl
apt-get install -y kubelet='1.37.1-*' kubectl='1.37.1-*'
apt-mark hold kubelet kubectl
systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart kubelet
kubectl uncordon cp1
```

**Verify:**

```bash
kubectl get nodes            # cp1 shows v1.37.1 and Ready
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | grep cp1   # control-plane Pods running
```

**Notes.** `upgrade apply` is right here because `cp1` is the first control-plane node; any other node would use `kubeadm upgrade node`. Drain before restarting the kubelet, and don't forget the uncordon: a node left `SchedulingDisabled` is a classic lost mark. If `kubectl` isn't configured as root on `cp1`, run drain and uncordon from wherever it is.

q: Take an etcd snapshot of the cluster to `/opt/etcd-backup.db` on the control-plane node.
a:
```bash
ssh cp1
sudo -i
grep -E 'trusted-ca-file|cert-file|key-file|listen-client-urls' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml

ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key \
  snapshot save /opt/etcd-backup.db
```

**Verify:**

```bash
ls -lh /opt/etcd-backup.db
etcdutl snapshot status /opt/etcd-backup.db -w table    # hash, revision, keys, size
```

**Notes.** Read the cert paths from the etcd manifest rather than trusting memory; labs sometimes move them. A restore uses `etcdutl snapshot restore … --data-dir <new dir>`, then points the etcd static Pod's data `hostPath` at that directory.

q: A new worker `node3` has kubeadm, kubelet and containerd installed. Join it to the cluster.
a:
```bash
# on the control plane: a fresh join command (tokens expire after 24h)
kubeadm token create --print-join-command

# on node3, as root, run exactly what it printed:
ssh node3
sudo kubeadm join 10.0.0.10:6443 --token <token> --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:<hash>
```

**Verify:**

```bash
kubectl get nodes          # node3 appears; Ready once the CNI DaemonSet Pod starts on it
```

**If the join fails**, the error is usually one of: swap still on, IP forwarding off (`sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward`), containerd not running, or the kubelet not installed at a matching version. `journalctl -u kubelet` on node3 shows the cause.

q: In namespace `ci`, create ServiceAccount `deployer`. It must be able to create, update and delete Deployments in `ci` only, and must not be able to read Secrets.
a:
```bash
k create sa deployer -n ci
k create role deployer -n ci --verb=get,list,watch,create,update,patch,delete --resource=deployments
k create rolebinding deployer -n ci --role=deployer --serviceaccount=ci:deployer
```

**Verify each clause:**

```bash
k auth can-i create deployments -n ci --as=system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer        # yes
k auth can-i delete deployments -n ci --as=system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer        # yes
k auth can-i create deployments -n default --as=system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer   # no
k auth can-i get secrets -n ci --as=system:serviceaccount:ci:deployer               # no
```

**Notes.** Role + RoleBinding keeps it in one namespace. The `--serviceaccount` value is `namespace:name`. A ClusterRoleBinding here would be the wrong answer, because it grants everywhere.

q: Install the chart `acme/web` (repository `https://charts.acme.example`) as release `shop` in a new namespace `shop`, with `replicaCount=3`. Then upgrade it to `replicaCount=4`, and roll back.
a:
```bash
helm repo add acme https://charts.acme.example
helm repo update
helm install shop acme/web -n shop --create-namespace --set replicaCount=3
helm upgrade shop acme/web -n shop --set replicaCount=4
helm history shop -n shop
helm rollback shop 1 -n shop
```

**Verify:**

```bash
helm list -n shop                # STATUS deployed, REVISION 3 (the rollback is a new revision)
helm get values shop -n shop     # replicaCount: 3 again
k get deploy -n shop
```

**Notes.** A rollback creates a *new* revision that copies an old one, so after install → upgrade → rollback, the history shows three revisions. Use the repository name and URL exactly as the task gives them.

q: Make sure only Pods that tolerate `dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule` can run on `worker3`, and that Deployment `trainer` (namespace `ml`) runs **only** on `worker3`.
a:
```bash
k taint node worker3 dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule
k label node worker3 dedicated=gpu
k edit deploy trainer -n ml
```

Add to the Pod template's `spec`:

```yaml
tolerations:
- { key: dedicated, operator: Equal, value: gpu, effect: NoSchedule }
nodeSelector:
  dedicated: gpu
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k get pods -n ml -l app=trainer -o wide       # NODE column: worker3 for every Pod
k describe node worker3 | grep -i taint
```

**Notes.** The taint keeps others off; the toleration *allows* trainer on; the nodeSelector (or node affinity) *sends* it there. Without the selector, trainer could still land anywhere.

q: Deployment `web` in `shop` must autoscale between 2 and 6 replicas, targeting 60% CPU. metrics-server is installed.
a:
```bash
k get deploy web -n shop -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources}'   # any CPU request?
k set resources deploy web -n shop --requests=cpu=200m   # only if there's no request yet
k autoscale deploy web -n shop --min=2 --max=6 --cpu-percent=60
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k get hpa -n shop               # TARGETS shows a number/60%, not <unknown>
k describe hpa web -n shop      # events explain scaling decisions
```

**Notes.** Utilisation is a percentage of the **request**, so without a CPU request the HPA can't compute anything. If your kubectl version suggests a newer flag spelling, `k autoscale --help` is the authority.

q: In namespace `shop`, only Pods labelled `app=frontend` may connect to Pods labelled `app=api`, and only on TCP 8080. Everything else to `api` must be blocked.
a:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: { name: api-allow-frontend, namespace: shop }
spec:
  podSelector: { matchLabels: { app: api } }
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector: { matchLabels: { app: frontend } }
    ports:
    - { protocol: TCP, port: 8080 }
```

**Verify from both sides:**

```bash
k run t1 -n shop --rm -it --image=busybox:1.36 --restart=Never -l app=frontend -- wget -qO- -T 3 http://api:8080   # works
k run t2 -n shop --rm -it --image=busybox:1.36 --restart=Never -- wget -qO- -T 3 http://api:8080                   # times out
```

**Notes.** Selecting `api` with an Ingress policy makes ingress to it deny-by-default, except what's listed. The `podSelector` under `from` without a `namespaceSelector` means the same namespace only. Testing with a labelled and an unlabelled Pod proves both halves.

q: Expose Service `api` (port 8080, namespace `shop`) at `http://shop.example.com/api` through the existing Gateway `main` in namespace `infra`, using the Gateway API.
a:
```yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: { name: shop-api, namespace: shop }
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - { name: main, namespace: infra }
  hostnames: ["shop.example.com"]
  rules:
  - matches:
    - path: { type: PathPrefix, value: /api }
    backendRefs:
    - { name: api, port: 8080 }
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k describe httproute shop-api -n shop      # Conditions: Accepted=True, ResolvedRefs=True
k get gateway main -n infra                # its address
curl -H 'Host: shop.example.com' http://<gateway-address>/api
```

**Notes.** If `Accepted` is False, check that the Gateway's listener allows routes from namespace `shop` (`allowedRoutes`) and that the hostname matches the listener. gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io is allowed during the CKA.

q: Create a PersistentVolume `pv-logs` (2Gi, RWO, `hostPath` `/mnt/logs`, class `manual`, Retain). Create PVC `logs` in `app` that binds to it, and mount it at `/var/log/app` in a new Pod `logger` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`).
a:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: { name: pv-logs }
spec:
  capacity: { storage: 2Gi }
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath: { path: /mnt/logs }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: { name: logs, namespace: app }
spec:
  storageClassName: manual
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: { requests: { storage: 2Gi } }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: logger, namespace: app }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: logger
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts: [{ name: logs, mountPath: /var/log/app }]
  volumes:
  - name: logs
    persistentVolumeClaim: { claimName: logs }
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k get pv pv-logs                 # STATUS Bound, CLAIM app/logs
k get pvc logs -n app            # Bound
k exec -n app logger -- sh -c 'echo ok > /var/log/app/t && cat /var/log/app/t'
```

**Notes.** Class, access mode and size must all be compatible for the bind. Using the same `storageClassName` on both makes the intent explicit and stops a default StorageClass from provisioning a different volume.

q: Node `worker2` is `NotReady`. Fix it so it's Ready, and make sure the fix survives a reboot.
a:
```bash
k describe node worker2 | sed -n '/Conditions/,/Addresses/p'
ssh worker2
sudo systemctl status kubelet          # inactive? failed? disabled?
sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 50 --no-pager
```

**Typical fixes, depending on what the journal says:**

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now kubelet                       # stopped and/or disabled
sudo vi /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml                      # a broken path or value
systemctl cat kubelet                                     # shows drop-ins and their paths
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart kubelet
sudo systemctl enable --now containerd                    # runtime down
```

**Verify:**

```bash
exit
k get nodes                   # worker2 Ready (may take ~30s)
```

**Notes.** "Survives a reboot" means `enable`, not just `start`. Read the journal before changing anything: exam faults are usually one deliberate typo, and the kubelet names it.

q: After a change, `kubectl` returns `connection refused`. The API server on `cp1` is down. Bring it back.
a:
```bash
ssh cp1
sudo -i
crictl ps -a | grep kube-apiserver           # Exited? restarting?
crictl logs <container-id> 2>&1 | tail -20    # the reason, e.g. a bad flag or missing file
ls /var/log/pods/ | grep apiserver           # logs survive here if the container is gone
cp /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml /root/apiserver.bak
vi /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml   # fix the flag/path/indentation it complained about
watch crictl ps                              # wait for kube-apiserver to be Running
```

**Verify:**

```bash
kubectl get nodes
kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-apiserver
```

**Notes.** Keep the backup **outside** the manifests directory. If there's no container at all, the kubelet couldn't parse the YAML: check indentation, and `journalctl -u kubelet` mentions the manifest.

q: Create Pod `web` in `apps` with an `nginx:1.27` container and a native sidecar `logger` (`busybox:1.36`) that runs `tail -F /var/log/nginx/access.log`. Both share an `emptyDir` mounted at `/var/log/nginx`.
a:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: web, namespace: apps }
spec:
  initContainers:
  - name: logger
    image: busybox:1.36
    restartPolicy: Always                 # makes it a native sidecar
    command: ["sh", "-c", "tail -F /var/log/nginx/access.log"]
    volumeMounts: [{ name: logs, mountPath: /var/log/nginx }]
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:1.27
    volumeMounts: [{ name: logs, mountPath: /var/log/nginx }]
  volumes:
  - name: logs
    emptyDir: {}
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k get pod web -n apps                       # READY 2/2
k exec -n apps web -c nginx -- curl -s localhost >/dev/null
k logs -n apps web -c logger                # the access-log line appears
```

**Notes.** If the task's cluster predates native sidecars, or the task says "add a second container", list the logger under `containers:` instead. Read the wording. Note that the nginx image's access.log is a symlink to stdout; mounting the `emptyDir` over `/var/log/nginx` replaces it with a real file the sidecar can tail.

q: Create a CronJob `cleanup` in `apps` that runs `busybox:1.36` with `echo cleaning` every 15 minutes, never runs two at once, and keeps only the last 2 successful Jobs. Then trigger one run immediately.
a:
```bash
k create cronjob cleanup -n apps --image=busybox:1.36 --schedule="*/15 * * * *" \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml -- sh -c 'echo cleaning' > cleanup.yaml
vi cleanup.yaml
```

Add under `spec:` (the CronJob's, not the Pod's):

```yaml
concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 2
```

```bash
k apply -f cleanup.yaml
k create job cleanup-now -n apps --from=cronjob/cleanup
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k get cronjob cleanup -n apps -o yaml | grep -E 'schedule|concurrencyPolicy|successfulJobsHistoryLimit'
k logs -n apps job/cleanup-now           # cleaning
```

q: Deployments `web-blue` (v1) and `web-green` (v2) run in `shop`; their Pods are labelled `app=web` plus `version=blue` or `version=green`. Service `web` currently sends traffic to blue. Switch all traffic to green with no downtime.
a:
```bash
k get pods -n shop -l app=web --show-labels        # confirm the labels
k get pods -n shop -l app=web,version=green        # green is Running and READY first
k patch svc web -n shop -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"web","version":"green"}}}'
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k get endpointslices -n shop -l kubernetes.io/service-name=web -o wide   # only green Pod IPs
k run t -n shop --rm -it --image=busybox:1.36 --restart=Never -- wget -qO- http://web
```

**Notes.** Check green is ready *before* the switch; that's what makes it zero-downtime. Leave blue running unless told to remove it, because it's your instant rollback.

q: Deployment `api` (4 replicas, Pods `app=api,track=stable`) sits behind Service `api` selecting `app=api`. Add a canary running `myapp:2.0` that gets roughly 20% of traffic.
a:
```bash
k get deploy api -n shop -o yaml > canary.yaml
vi canary.yaml
#   metadata.name: api-canary ; replicas: 1
#   selector.matchLabels and template labels: app: api, track: canary
#   container image: myapp:2.0 ; remove status, uid, resourceVersion, creationTimestamp
k apply -f canary.yaml
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k get pods -n shop -l app=api -L track                 # 4 stable + 1 canary
k get endpointslices -n shop -l kubernetes.io/service-name=api -o wide   # 5 endpoints
```

**Notes.** One canary out of five Pods gives about 20%, per connection. The Service's selector (`app=api`) must match both tracks, while each Deployment's own selector must include `track` so the two Deployments don't fight over each other's Pods.

q: Deployment `api` (port 8080) restarts constantly. It takes about 60 seconds to start, and its liveness probe begins after 5 seconds. Fix it so it starts reliably, gets traffic only when `/ready` succeeds, and is still restarted if `/healthz` fails once it's running.
a:
```yaml
# in the container spec
startupProbe:
  httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: 8080 }
  periodSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 24        # up to 120s to start
readinessProbe:
  httpGet: { path: /ready, port: 8080 }
  periodSeconds: 5
livenessProbe:
  httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: 8080 }
  periodSeconds: 10
  failureThreshold: 3
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k rollout status deploy/api -n shop
k get pods -n shop -l app=api          # RESTARTS stops climbing; READY 1/1 after startup
k describe pod -n shop -l app=api | grep -A3 -E 'Liveness|Readiness|Startup'
```

**Notes.** The startupProbe gives the slow start its own budget, so the liveness probe can stay strict. Raising the liveness `initialDelaySeconds` would also work, but it delays failure detection for the Pod's whole life.

q: Create Pod `secure` in `apps` using image `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27` (it listens on 8080 and writes only under `/tmp`). It must run as user 101, be unable to escalate privileges, drop all capabilities and have a read-only root filesystem.
a:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: secure, namespace: apps }
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsUser: 101
    runAsNonRoot: true
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27
    ports: [{ containerPort: 8080 }]
    securityContext:
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
    volumeMounts:
    - { name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp }
  volumes:
  - { name: tmp, emptyDir: {} }
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k get pod secure -n apps                         # Running
k exec -n apps secure -- id                      # uid=101
k exec -n apps secure -- touch /test             # Read-only file system
k exec -n apps secure -- curl -s localhost:8080 | head -3
```

**Notes.** A read-only root filesystem needs a writable `emptyDir` wherever the app genuinely writes, here `/tmp`. If it crash-loops, `k logs` names the path it couldn't write, and that tells you which mount is missing. Stock `nginx` would fail as user 101, because it binds port 80 and writes under `/var/cache/nginx`. That's why unprivileged images exist.

q: Namespace `team` must be limited to 2 CPU and 4Gi memory in requests, and any container created without requests should get 100m CPU and 128Mi memory automatically.
a:
```bash
k create quota team-q -n team --hard=requests.cpu=2,requests.memory=4Gi
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata: { name: defaults, namespace: team }
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Container
    defaultRequest: { cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi }
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k describe quota team-q -n team
k run probe -n team --image=nginx:1.27
k get pod probe -n team -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].resources}'   # requests filled in
```

**Notes.** Without the LimitRange, the quota would reject every Pod that doesn't declare requests. The two work as a pair.

q: kube-bench reports that the kubelet on `worker1` allows anonymous requests and uses `AlwaysAllow` authorization. Fix both.
a:
```bash
ssh worker1
sudo vi /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
```

```yaml
authentication:
  anonymous: { enabled: false }
  webhook: { enabled: true }
authorization:
  mode: Webhook
```

```bash
sudo systemctl restart kubelet
sudo systemctl status kubelet        # active (running)
```

**Verify:**

```bash
kube-bench run --targets node 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'anonymous|authorization'   # now PASS
exit; k get nodes                                                              # worker1 Ready
```

q: ServiceAccount `default` in namespace `web` must no longer mount API tokens into Pods, and Deployment `site` (which never calls the API) must run with its own ServiceAccount `site` that has no RBAC bindings.
a:
```bash
k patch sa default -n web -p '{"automountServiceAccountToken": false}'
k create sa site -n web
k patch sa site -n web -p '{"automountServiceAccountToken": false}'
k set serviceaccount deploy/site site -n web
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k get pods -n web -l app=site -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.serviceAccountName}'          # site
k exec -n web deploy/site -- ls /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount 2>&1        # No such file
k auth can-i --list -n web --as=system:serviceaccount:web:site | head                     # only the basics
```

q: The AppArmor profile file `/opt/k8s-deny-write` exists on `worker1`. Load it, and run Pod `writer` (image `busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) in `default` confined by it.
a:
```bash
ssh worker1
sudo apparmor_parser -q /opt/k8s-deny-write
sudo aa-status | grep k8s            # note the exact profile NAME it prints
exit
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: writer }
spec:
  nodeName: worker1
  containers:
  - name: writer
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    securityContext:
      appArmorProfile:
        type: Localhost
        localhostProfile: k8s-deny-write      # the name from aa-status
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k exec writer -- cat /proc/1/attr/current     # k8s-deny-write (enforce)
k exec writer -- touch /tmp/x                 # Permission denied
```

**Notes.** The profile is only loaded on worker1, so the Pod must run there (`nodeName` or a nodeSelector). Use the name declared inside the profile, which may differ from the filename.

q: Namespace `payments` must reject any new Pod that doesn't meet the `restricted` Pod Security Standard. Then fix Deployment `checkout` so its Pods are admitted.
a:
```bash
k label ns payments pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version=latest --overwrite
k rollout restart deploy/checkout -n payments
k get events -n payments --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | grep -i podsecurity   # what's violated
k edit deploy checkout -n payments
```

Add to the Pod template:

```yaml
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    seccompProfile: { type: RuntimeDefault }
  containers:
  - name: checkout
    securityContext:
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k rollout status deploy/checkout -n payments
k get pods -n payments                 # new Pods Running
```

**Notes.** The label alone doesn't touch running Pods. The restart is what surfaces the violations, which the events list precisely. If the image runs as root, `runAsNonRoot` also needs a numeric `runAsUser` (or a non-root image).

q: Enable encryption at rest for Secrets using `aescbc`, keep existing Secrets readable, and make sure every existing Secret ends up encrypted.
a:
```bash
ssh cp1 ; sudo -i
mkdir -p /etc/kubernetes/enc
head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64            # the key
cat > /etc/kubernetes/enc/enc.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1
kind: EncryptionConfiguration
resources:
- resources: ["secrets"]
  providers:
  - aescbc:
      keys:
      - name: key1
        secret: <paste the base64 key>
  - identity: {}
YAML
cp /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml /root/
vi /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
#   - --encryption-provider-config=/etc/kubernetes/enc/enc.yaml
#   volumeMounts:  - { name: enc, mountPath: /etc/kubernetes/enc, readOnly: true }
#   volumes:       - { name: enc, hostPath: { path: /etc/kubernetes/enc, type: DirectoryOrCreate } }
watch crictl ps                              # wait for the apiserver
kubectl get secrets -A -o json | kubectl replace -f -
```

**Verify:**

```bash
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key \
  get /registry/secrets/default/<some-secret> | hexdump -C | head   # k8s:enc:aescbc:v1:key1
```

**Notes.** `aescbc` first means new writes are encrypted; `identity` second keeps old plain-text data readable until it's rewritten. The volume mount is essential, or the API server can't read the file and won't start.

q: Pods in namespace `web` must only use images from `registry.example.com/`. Enforce it without a webhook.
a:
```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata: { name: web-registry }
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources: ["pods"]
  validations:
  - expression: "object.spec.containers.all(c, c.image.startsWith('registry.example.com/'))"
    message: "images in web must come from registry.example.com"
---
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata: { name: web-registry }
spec:
  policyName: web-registry
  validationActions: ["Deny"]
  matchResources:
    namespaceSelector:
      matchLabels: { kubernetes.io/metadata.name: web }
```

**Verify:**

```bash
k run ok  -n web --image=registry.example.com/nginx:1.27 --dry-run=server   # allowed
k run bad -n web --image=nginx:1.27 --dry-run=server                        # denied, with your message
```

**Notes.** `--dry-run=server` runs admission without creating anything, which is perfect for testing policies. To also cover init containers, extend the CEL expression to check `object.spec.initContainers` when present.

q: Find the Pods in namespace `legacy` whose images have CRITICAL vulnerabilities, according to Trivy, and delete only those Pods.
a:
```bash
k get pods -n legacy -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.spec.containers[*].image}{"\n"}{end}'

for img in $(k get pods -n legacy -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.containers[*].image}' | tr ' ' '\n' | sort -u); do
  echo "== $img"; trivy image --severity CRITICAL --quiet "$img" | grep -E 'Total|CRITICAL' | head -3
done

k delete pod <pod-a> <pod-b> -n legacy      # only the ones whose images had CRITICAL findings
```

**Verify:** `k get pods -n legacy` shows only the clean Pods remaining.

**Notes.** List first, decide, then delete exactly those. Deleting extra Pods is graded as wrong too. If a Pod belongs to a Deployment it will come back, so read whether the task wants the Pod or its controller removed.

q: Configure API server auditing: log Secret changes in `RequestResponse`, everything else in `Metadata`, to `/var/log/kubernetes/audit/audit.log`, keeping 2 backups of at most 50 MB.
a:
```bash
ssh cp1 ; sudo -i
mkdir -p /etc/kubernetes/audit /var/log/kubernetes/audit
cat > /etc/kubernetes/audit/policy.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1
kind: Policy
omitStages: ["RequestReceived"]
rules:
- level: RequestResponse
  resources: [{ group: "", resources: ["secrets"] }]
  verbs: ["create", "update", "patch", "delete"]
- level: Metadata
YAML
cp /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml /root/
vi /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
```

Add:

```yaml
- --audit-policy-file=/etc/kubernetes/audit/policy.yaml
- --audit-log-path=/var/log/kubernetes/audit/audit.log
- --audit-log-maxbackup=2
- --audit-log-maxsize=50
# volumeMounts:
- { name: audit-policy, mountPath: /etc/kubernetes/audit/policy.yaml, readOnly: true }
- { name: audit-log, mountPath: /var/log/kubernetes/audit/ }
# volumes:
- { name: audit-policy, hostPath: { path: /etc/kubernetes/audit/policy.yaml, type: File } }
- { name: audit-log, hostPath: { path: /var/log/kubernetes/audit/, type: DirectoryOrCreate } }
```

**Verify:**

```bash
watch crictl ps                                   # apiserver back
kubectl create secret generic audit-test --from-literal=a=b
grep audit-test /var/log/kubernetes/audit/audit.log | tail -1 | jq .level   # "RequestResponse"
```

**Notes.** Specific rule first, catch-all last (first match wins). Missing volume mounts are the number-one reason the API server won't come back.

q: Falco is running on `worker1`. Change the rule `Terminal shell in container` so its output is `%evt.time,%container.id,%proc.name`, then identify the Pod that triggers it.
a:
```bash
ssh worker1 ; sudo -i
grep -n -A12 'rule: Terminal shell in container' /etc/falco/falco_rules.yaml   # copy the rule
vi /etc/falco/falco_rules.local.yaml
```

Paste the whole rule into the local file and change only its output:

```yaml
- rule: Terminal shell in container
  desc: A shell was used as the entrypoint/exec point into a container with an attached terminal.
  condition: <unchanged, copied from the default rule>
  output: "%evt.time,%container.id,%proc.name"
  priority: NOTICE
```

```bash
systemctl list-units | grep falco          # find the unit name
systemctl restart falco-modern-bpf         # (use the name it printed)
journalctl -u falco-modern-bpf -f          # wait for a line: time,<container-id>,bash
crictl ps --id <container-id>              # POD column names the Pod
crictl inspect <container-id> | grep -E 'io.kubernetes.pod.(name|namespace)'
```

**Notes.** Overriding in `falco_rules.local.yaml` replaces the rule of the same name and survives Falco updates. Copy the condition exactly; only the output was asked to change. Recent Falco versions also accept an `override:` block that replaces just the `output` field. falco.org/docs ("Rules → Overriding") shows both styles.
